name: Dark Lime
lede: Dark Lime is a deep, saturated yellow-green, a shade down from [[lime]] and classed by the ISCC-NBS system as a vivid yellow green.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
No book in our library records a name at this position before the xkcd color survey of 2010, where the public supplied the plain descriptive phrase "dark lime" [1]. Its origin before that survey is undocumented here [1].

The nearest ISCC-NBS 1955 block is vivid yellow green, about 6 CIEDE2000 units away, and the closest Munsell reading runs near 6.0GY in hue [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[avocado]], [[acid-green]] and [[avocado-green]], at 3.5, 4.3 and 4.5 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a match for this swatch in just one of 23,781 paintings, Paul Gauguin's *Mother and Child under a Tree at Pont-Aven* (1886), where it covers about 5 per cent of the canvas [2]. That single hit is in a French painting, giving France a far higher than average rate for this exact shade in our small sample [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so one hit says the shade is rare on surviving canvas, not that it was rarely mixed [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[2].
